description: DeepFlood for Inundated Vegetation High-Resolution Dataset for Accurate Flood Mapping and Segmentation is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Mulham Fawakherji et al. Rapid and accurate assessment of flood extent is important for effective disaster response, mitigation planning, and resource allocation. Traditional flood mapping methods encounter challenges in scalability and transferability. However, the emergence of deep learning, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), supports flood mapping by learning spatial patterns and semantic features directly from raw data. Coverage: not stated; published in 2025. Formats: GeoTIFF, Shapefile, Image. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 4859203529 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
